analysis.summary: Transmit Unicode text in byte-limited chunks with headers, respecting segment boundaries and budget constraints.

traps.quote: The request budget B limits total wire bytes: payload bytes plus headers.
traps.consequence: Computing chunks * H overflows i64 when both values are near 10^18 bounds.
traps.guard: Recognize worst case: N segments, each its own chunk; use u64 or overflow-safe arithmetic for wire_bytes.

traps.quote: A chunk cannot cross a source-segment boundary. Reaching that boundary closes it.
traps.consequence: Chunks span segments if boundaries are not forced to close; wrong character and chunk counts.
traps.guard: Compute segment boundaries as cumulative character positions; force chunk closure when last char of segment is reached.

traps.quote: Next S positive integers: source-segment lengths whose sum is N.
traps.consequence: Treating segment lengths as byte counts instead of character counts shifts all boundary positions.
traps.guard: Segment lengths are character counts matching N; accumulate as character positions, not bytes.

traps.quote: If this would exceed B, stop before that character. A header is never sent without at least one character.
traps.consequence: Outputting non-zero chunks, payload, or wire_bytes when first character + header exceeds B.
traps.guard: Check if width(L) + H > B before any transmission; if true, set last=0, chunks=0, cause=LIMIT immediately.

traps.quote: Before sending a character, include its payload width and, if it would begin a new chunk, one header. If this would exceed B, stop before that character.
traps.consequence: Off-by-one: transmitting one character too many or too few if budget check uses >= instead of >.
traps.guard: Check current_wire + char_width + (H if new_chunk) > B strictly; stop if true without sending character.

traps.quote: with one-based positions and 1 <= L <= R <= N
traps.consequence: Off-by-one errors in converting one-based L, R to zero-based array indices; wrong character range processed.
traps.guard: Consistently convert L, R to zero-based by subtracting 1; document and verify at every access point.

analysis.input_shape: Character count N, segment count S, query count Q, chunk size C, header cost H, budget B; characters as hex; segment lengths summing to N; queries with one-based range [L,R] and budget.
analysis.output_shape: Seven space-separated integers per query: payload_bytes wire_bytes characters last chunks last_chunk_payload_bytes cause.
invariants: Segment boundary forces chunk closure even if chunk not full.
No chunk spans a segment boundary or exceeds C payload bytes.
Header H is charged once per chunk; stop if adding next character exceeds budget B.

verification.ambiguity_note: Candidates written from different readings of the statement do not agree: {adversarial} | {complexity, edgefirst, literal, plain, restate, traps}. Divergence across framings points at an ambiguity in the statement rather than at a typo, so the clause involved was re-read rather than resolved by majority.
